name: Radiance-field optimization
text:
# Radiance-field optimization


## Overview
Radiance-field optimization is a family of inverse rendering methods that reconstruct a 3D scene representation by minimizing the photometric error between rendered images and ground-truth observations [S2]. It solves the problem of novel view synthesis by training a neural network to directly learn color and opacity (or density) values using the discrete [volume rendering equation](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md) [S2]. Unlike explicit mesh-based reconstruction, radiance-field optimization relies on the differentiability of the forward volume rendering operator to propagate gradients from pixel space to the scene representation [G].

## Shared principles
See [Differentiable and inverse volume rendering](42-differentiable-and-inverse-volume-rendering.md) for shared principles.

## Subtopics

### [Hierarchical Grid Optimization](1414-hierarchical-grid-optimization.md)
Optimizes explicit 3D voxel grids to reconstruct radiance fields, solving the computational bottleneck of implicit neural networks by replacing them with direct data access and interpolation. Chosen when memory efficiency and direct grid manipulation are prioritized over implicit representations.

### [3D Gaussian Splatting](1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md)
Represents a scene as a collection of anisotropic 3D Gaussian primitives defined by mean position, covariance, opacity, and [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md). Chosen for real-time rendering and high-fidelity novel view synthesis, setting itself apart by using explicit differentiable primitives instead of implicit MLPs or dense grids.

### [Neural Transient Fields (NeTF)](4760-neural-transient-fields-netf.md)
Models the plenoptic transient field using an MLP to predict transient arrival times from sparse SPAD measurements for Non-Line-of-Sight imaging. Chosen for NLOS scenarios where sparse temporal data is available, differing from [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) by operating on transient fields rather than static radiance.

### [Neural Radiance Fields](4972-neural-radiance-fields.md)
Represents a 3D scene as a continuous volumetric function parameterized by a neural network, mapping 3D coordinates and viewing directions to RGB color and density. Chosen as the foundational implicit representation for novel view synthesis, setting itself apart by enabling photorealistic rendering of complex scenes with view-dependent effects.

### [SNeRG](5976-snerg.md)
Reduces [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) computational cost by decomposing the radiance field into density, diffuse RGB, and feature vectors, using deferred shading to limit MLP evaluations. Chosen when inference speed is critical, differing from standard NeRF by caching geometry and using a small network for view-dependent effects.

### [NeRF++](6198-nerf.md)
Jointly optimizes camera parameters (intrinsics and 6DoF poses) and the scene representation from sparse forward-facing RGB images. Chosen when camera poses are unknown, setting itself apart by eliminating the need for pre-computed SfM parameters.

### [Generalized Rendering Models](6681-generalized-rendering-models.md)
Trains deep neural architectures end-to-end to optimize volume rendering parameters for clinical data with high inter-patient variations. Chosen for medical imaging applications, differing from manual transfer functions by learning consistent visual outputs across subjects.

### [Optimization Procedures](7150-optimization-procedures.md)
Defines iterative procedures that minimize [photometric loss](#9563-photometric-loss-rawnerf-variant.md) by updating scene parameters. Chosen to manage training dynamics, ray sampling, and hyperparameter scheduling, addressing the ill-posed nature of inverse volume rendering.

### [Simple-RF](7279-simple-rf.md)
A regularization framework for sparse-input radiance fields that constrains the main model to learn simpler solutions by supervising it with depth estimates from lower-capacity versions. Chosen for sparse-view reconstruction, setting itself apart from methods like 3DGS by using self-supervision for regularization.

### [VDN-NeRF](7383-vdn-nerf.md)
Trains NeRFs for better geometry under non-Lambertian surfaces and dynamic lighting by normalizing view-dependence through self-distillation. Chosen to resolve shape-radiance ambiguity, differing from standard NeRF by encoding invariant information.

### [DeRF (Decomposed Radiance Fields)](7673-derf-decomposed-radiance-fields.md)
Mitigates high computational cost by spatially decomposing a scene into multiple parts, each represented by a smaller neural network. Chosen for large scenes requiring near-constant inference time, setting itself apart by using differentiable spatial partitioning.

### [Dual Rendering Equation Optimization](8167-dual-rendering-equation-optimization.md)
A differentiable technique that jointly optimizes scene parameters by minimizing a [combined loss](#4177-total-loss-function.md) from volumetric emission-absorption and surface reflectance models. Chosen for scenes requiring both [volumetric and surface](#9530-k-sdf.md) modeling, differing by using a dual rendering equation.

### [Planar Reflection-Aware NeRF](8312-planar-reflection-aware-nerf.md)
A NeRF variant that jointly models planar reflectors and explicitly casts reflected rays to capture high-frequency reflections. Chosen for indoor scenes with windows/mirrors, setting itself apart by preventing false geometry along primary rays.

### [Tetra-NeRF](8932-tetra-nerf.md)
Replaces uniform voxel grids or sparse point clouds with a dense set of non-overlapping tetrahedra from Delaunay triangulation. Chosen to solve empty regions in sparse methods and fixed resolution limits, differing by using a tetrahedral mesh.

### [Light Field and Lumigraph Methods](9271-light-field-and-lumigraph-methods.md)
Synthesizes novel views by leveraging dense sampling of light rays from multiple viewpoints, either through explicit discretization or implicit neural representations. Chosen for [light-field based rendering](#9271-light-field-and-lumigraph-methods.md), differing from global [implicit fields](#1800-implicit-surface-primitives.md) by focusing on ray sampling.

### [Generalizable Radiance Fields](9480-generalizable-radiance-fields.md)
Not given in the sources.

### [General Radiance Field (GRF)](9638-general-radiance-field-grf.md)
Implicitly represents and renders 3D scenes by learning local features for each pixel in 2D images and projecting them to 3D space. Chosen for general 3D representation and rendering, setting itself apart by constructing an internal representation for every 3D point.

### [Closed-Form Color Field Estimation](10574-closed-form-color-field-estimation.md)
Computes the color field solely from a given density field and posed training images in closed form. Chosen to decouple shape and radiance, reducing shape-radiance ambiguity inherent in NeRF.

### [Surface-SDF Representation](10778-surface-sdf-representation.md)
Reconstructs 3D geometry and appearance by modeling the scene as a continuous implicit surface defined by a Signed Distance Function ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)). Chosen to disentangle geometry from appearance, enabling high-fidelity surface reconstruction.

### [Neural Illumination Fields (NeIF)](10930-neural-illumination-fields-neif.md)
Represents 3D ambient illumination as a continuous volumetric radiance field, treating each sample as a light emitter. Chosen for fully differentiable illumination modeling, differing by integrating volumetric radiance along specular lobes.

### [NeRF-XL Joint Training](10947-nerf-xl-joint-training.md)
Distributes NeRF parameters across multiple GPUs by allocating them to disjoint spatial regions and training them jointly. Chosen for arbitrarily large capacity without redundancy, setting itself apart from independent training methods.

### [Physical and Material Priors](11198-physical-and-material-priors.md)
Extends standard optimization by incorporating physical laws (e.g., ray refraction) or material properties (e.g., BRDFs) into the pipeline. Chosen for [physically-based rendering](#6815-physically-based-rendering-pbr-lighting.md), differing by enforcing physical constraints.

### [LiDAR-NeRF](11289-lidar-nerf.md)
A differentiable framework for novel LiDAR view synthesis that jointly learns geometry and 3D point attributes without explicit reconstruction. Chosen for LiDAR-based scene representation, differing by handling distance, intensity, and ray-drop probability.

### [Deformable and Dynamic Fields](11311-deformable-and-dynamic-fields.md)
Extends static optimization to model scenes that change over time or undergo non-rigid deformation [912-neural-volumes.md][5540-endonerf.md]. Chosen for dynamic scenes, setting itself apart by introducing temporal or deformation components.

### [HDR-NeRF](11334-hdr-nerf.md)
Recovers a high dynamic range radiance field from low dynamic range views with different exposures. Chosen for HDR synthesis, differing by enabling generation of novel HDR and LDR views under arbitrary exposures.

### [GNeuVox](11357-gneuvox.md)
A differentiable framework for fast human radiance field optimization that replaces implicit MLPs with explicit [neural voxel grids](#2159-voxelgrid.md). Chosen to accelerate training from hours to minutes, setting itself apart by maintaining two separate voxel grids.

### [NeRFifyMesh](11365-nerfifymesh.md)
Converts textured [mesh models](#8738-voxelblockymodelmesh.md) into NeRFs by generating a ground-truth [point-based radiance field](#7366-differentiable-point-based-radiance-fields.md) from mesh geometry and texture. Chosen for mesh-to-NeRF conversion, differing by eliminating the need for multi-view image rendering.

### [Progressively Deblurring Radiance Field (PDRF)](11382-progressively-deblurring-radiance-field-pdrf.md)
Reconstructs high-quality radiance fields from blurry images by incorporating 3D scene context into blur modeling and using efficient [importance sampling](#9521-importance-sampling.md). Chosen for deblurring applications, differing by modeling blur with scene context.

### [Geometry Pseudo Label via Image Warping](11450-geometry-pseudo-label-via-image-warping.md)
Reconstructs reasonable 3D geometry from a single reference view by propagating depth information to unseen views through image warping. Chosen to prevent overfitting and collapse in single-view reconstruction, differing by using pseudo ground truth labels.

### [Canonical Neural Radiance Field for X-ray Tomography](11451-canonical-neural-radiance-field-for-x-ray-tomography.md)
Encodes the 3D density field of a static object using a NeRF, trained on rich projection data to serve as a prior for dynamic reconstruction. Chosen for X-ray tomography, differing by using a canonical volume prior.

### [Tensorial and Low-Rank Representations](11617-tensorial-and-low-rank-representations.md)
Addresses high memory consumption and overfitting in dense voxel-based fields by modeling the scene as a factorized 4D tensor [3026-tensorf.md]. Chosen for compact modeling, differing by using low-rank tensor [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md).

### [Hybrid Explicit-Implicit Representations](12240-hybrid-explicit-implicit-representations.md)
Not given in the sources.

### [Explicit Voxel/Grid Representations](12527-explicit-voxel-grid-representations.md)
Optimizes scene parameters stored in discrete 3D grids or hierarchical structures, avoiding implicit MLP parameterization [4972-neural-radiance-fields.md]. Chosen for direct data access and interpolation, differing by optimizing explicit grids directly.

### [Neural Residual Field (ReRF)](12546-neural-residual-field-rerf.md)
Generates compact neural representations of dynamic scenes from RGB video by sequentially optimizing explicit feature, motion, and residual grids. Chosen for dynamic scene [compression](#4-compression.md), differing by using sequential grid optimization.

### [Neural 3D Volume Decomposition](12553-neural-3d-volume-decomposition.md)
Optimizes a 3D neural volume with shape and SVBRDF while also optimizing per-image illuminations. Chosen for varying illumination and viewpoints, differing by decomposing volume, shape, and lighting.

### [Shading-Guided NeRF Synthesis](12837-shading-guided-nerf-synthesis.md)
Synthesizes large-scale NeRF scenes from a smaller exemplar by controlling lighting effects using shading vectors. Chosen for large-scale synthesis without decoupling geometry, material, and lighting, differing by using shading vectors.

### Nerflets
Nerflets achieves efficient structure-aware 3D scene representation with only 2D supervision by representing a scene as a set of local [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) (Nerflets), each with orientation, spatial position, and range [S5]. For a sampled point, N small MLPs generate N densities and colors, one for each Nerflet [S5]. The final color and density of the sampled point are obtained through weighted averaging based on the influence weights of each Nerflet [S5]. On KITTI-360 and ScanNet datasets, PSNR is more than one point higher [S5].

### General Radiance Field Rendering via MLP
[General Radiance Field](#9638-general-radiance-field-grf.md) Rendering via MLP is an MLP that predicts RGB values and volumetric density for a 3D point using its aggregated feature vector and viewing direction, forming a general radiance field [S6]. The steps are: Render an image pixel RGB by casting a ray from the camera center and estimating the integral using volume rendering equations with numerical quadrature [S6]. Estimate the integrals with numerical quadrature using a hierarchical sampling strategy, strictly following NeRF [S6]. All 3D locations and RGB values are processed by the [positional encoding](#876-positional-encoding.md) proposed by NeRF [S6]. Optimization uses [L2 loss](#6038-mean-square-error-mse.md) between rendered RGBs and ground truth [S6]. Unlike original NeRF which uses point position xyz as input, this method uses the aggregated point features $\bar{F}_p$ as input to the MLP [S6].

### Semantic Pseudo Label with Global Structure Prior
Semantic Pseudo Label with Global Structure Prior uses a global structure prior using a pre-trained [Vision Transformer](#10441-transformers-and-vision-transformers-vit.md) (ViT) to enforce semantic consistency between unseen views and the reference view, robust to pixel-wise misalignment [S7]. Unlike DietNeRF which uses projected image embeddings, directly extract the [CLS] token from DINO-ViT’s output as it serves as a representation of an entire image [S7]. Calculate L2 distance between extracted features: $\mathcal{L}_{\text{cls}} = ||f_{\text{vit}}(A) - f_{\text{vit}}(B) ||^2$, where $f_{vit}(\cdot)$ refers to the extracted [CLS] tokens, and A and B are patches from the reference view and an unseen view, respectively [S7]. The method adopts DINO-ViT [4], a self-supervised vision transformer trained on ImageNet [8] dataset [S7].

### iVR-GS
iVR-GS is a method for real-time editing of transfer functions and lighting during [neural volume rendering](#1576-neural-volume-rendering.md) using editable and composable 3DGS primitives, overcoming the limitation of baked visual parameters [S8, unofficial]. Steps: 1. Compose multiple basic models trained on disjoint transfer function ranges [S8, unofficial]. 2. Extend Gaussian primitives with [normals and shading](#1831-normal-shading.md) coefficients [S8, unofficial]. 3. Incorporate Blinn-Phong reflection. 4. Enable real-time editing of color, opacity, and lighting at inference [S8, unofficial]. 5. Perform automatic optimization to approximate reference images [S8, unofficial]. Pitfalls: Model size scales linearly with the number of basic scenes, reaching gigabyte-level for hundreds of transfer functions [S8, unofficial]. Uses uniform viewpoint sampling which may be suboptimal [S8, unofficial]. Requires redesigning lighting representation for models beyond Blinn-Phong [S8, unofficial]. Reconstruction quality: PSNR approximately 32–34 dB for novel view synthesis, 30–33 dB for relighting [S8, unofficial]. Compression: [Vector quantization](#907-vector-quantization.md) achieved 7.2× compression (6.2 MB vs. 44.8 MB) while maintaining accuracy within 0.06 dB [S8, unofficial].

### R2L
[R2L](#8670-r2l-neural-light-field.md) is a method distilling neural radiance fields into [neural light fields](#9273-neural-light-field-representations.md) via a deep residual MLP to improve [rendering efficiency](#12180-sorting-and-rendering-pipeline-optimization.md) [S9]. Train by distilling from a pre-trained NeRF [S9]. Achieves 26–35× reduction in FLOPs [S9]. Achieves 28–31× speedup in wall-clock time [S9].

### EG3D
EG3D is a GAN framework using a novel hybrid tri-plane representation for neural rendering, achieving state-of-the-art results on FFHQ [S9].

### Radiance-Driven Fluid Simulation
Radiance-Driven Fluid Simulation is a joint training framework where the fluid simulator is learned from video supervision by backpropagating the error between rendered images and ground-truth video frames through the differentiable renderer to the simulator [S10, unofficial]. Steps: Advect the volume field $V_t$ using the velocity field $u_t$ inferred by the simulator to get the updated volume field $V_{t+1}$ [S10, unofficial]. Assign the updated volume field $V_{t+1}$ into the scene space to render image $\hat{I}_{t+1}$ [S10, unofficial]. Supervise the rendered image $\hat{I}_{t+1}$ with the ground-truth image $I_{t+1}$ to update simulator parameters [S10, unofficial]. Pre-train the radiance field network with the initial volume field of all training sequences (volume of first frames) before joint training [S10, unofficial]. Formulas: $V_{t+1} = \text{advect}(u_t, \Delta t, V_t)$ [S10, unofficial]. $L = \sum_r \|\hat{C}(r) - C(r)\|_2^2 + \beta \|\nabla \cdot u\|_2^2$, where $\beta$ controls regularization strength [S10, unofficial]. Parameter: $\beta$: Regularization strength for divergence penalty, set to $1e-6$ [S10, unofficial].

### Online Learning for Irradiance Volumes
Online Learning for Irradiance Volumes updates a learned irradiance cache at runtime, extending surface-based neural caching to full volumetric scene representations [S11]. Steps: Initialize online learning from a previously learned NIV to significantly improve convergence compared to learning from scratch [S11]. To achieve real-time updates, restrict sampling to the camera's view frustum and/or employ loss-driven sampling [DPD22] [S11]. Pitfall: Inherently slower to learn than surface methods due to a larger input domain (entire scene volume vs. surface subset) and the requirement for a low-bias representation to avoid deferring queries [S11].

### 3DGS Radiance Caching
3DGS Radiance Caching is a caching technique for path-traced volume rendering that uses 3DGS primitives to store attenuated radiance at multiple path lengths, optimizing exponentially subsampled Gaussians from noisy path samples to achieve real-time frame rates [S8, unofficial]. Parameter: Memory footprint: 28 MB for the cache, compared to 272 MB for [neural radiance caching](#9347-neural-radiance-caching.md) [S8, unofficial]. Pitfall: Introduces bias with no guaranteed error bounds and requires re-initialization when transfer functions change [S8, unofficial]. Performance on six scientific datasets at 720p: real-time frame rates achieved with 38–186ms total time [S8, unofficial].

## Background
Radiance-field optimization emerged as a dominant paradigm for novel view synthesis following the introduction of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) by Mildenhall et al. in 2021 [S2]. Prior to this, image-based rendering relied on light-field sampling or explicit geometry reconstruction [S2]. NeRF demonstrated that a continuous volumetric function, optimized via gradient descent to minimize photometric error, could synthesize photorealistic images from sparse views [S2]. The field has since expanded to include explicit representations like voxel grids [4694-direct-voxel-grid-optimization.md] and Gaussian splats [1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md], as well as applications in dynamic scenes [912-neural-volumes.md], medical imaging [S5], and non-optical domains like radar [8904-radar-fields.md].
